tor.level.bulletSaferMedia: WebGL is off; audio and video play only after a click.
tor.level.bulletAllJs: JavaScript is off on all sites.
tor.level.bulletSafestMedia: Web fonts, audio, video and WebGL are off.
tor.level.applyTitle: Reopen Tor tabs to apply it?
tor.level.applyBody: Open Tor tabs keep the previous level until they reopen. They reopen at the same pages; sites may ask you to sign in again.
tor.level.stale: Open Tor tabs still use the previous level
tor.level.notSaved: The security level couldn’t be saved. Try again.
tor.circuit.none: No circuit yet. It appears once the page has started loading.
tor.circuit.unavailable: The circuit can’t be read right now.
tor.circuit.onion: An onion service keeps its own relays hidden. This is your side of the connection.
tor.download.title: Be careful opening downloads
tor.download.body: Some files connect to the internet when you open them, and that happens outside Tor. To stay safe, open them while offline or on a system that always uses Tor, like Tails.
tor.download.openTitle: Open a file from a Tor tab?
tor.settings.notSaved: This Tor setting couldn’t be saved. Try again.
tor.onion.open: Open the .onion version of this site
tor.onion.tooltip: This site is also an onion service. Open its .onion address.
tor.onion.preferDetail: When a site you open in a Tor tab names its onion address, open that instead. The first request still goes to the regular address.
tor.onionAuth.titleMissing: This onion site needs a key
tor.onionAuth.bodyMissing: The owner of {site} limits who can open it. Paste the private key they gave you.
tor.onionAuth.bodyWrong: {site} refused the key. Check that you pasted the whole key made for this site, then try again.
tor.onionAuth.label: Private key
tor.onionAuth.note: The key stays in memory and is forgotten when Acira closes. It is never written to disk.
tor.onionAuth.badKey: That doesn’t look like an onion service key. It is 52 letters and digits, or one line of an .auth_private file.
tor.onionAuth.refused: Tor didn’t accept the key. Try again.
privacy.passkeysDetail: Let sites ask Windows for a passkey or security key. When off, sites use your password instead.
privacy.passkeysReload: Reload pages that are already open to use passkeys on them.
update.noNotes: This update brings fixes and improvements.
pwp.note.encrypted.mac: Passwords are encrypted with a key macOS keeps for your account. Showing, copying, exporting and editing ask macOS to verify you first.
pwp.exportCsvDetail.mac: macOS verifies it’s you first. The file holds every password in plain text.
passwords.seeCopyEditOrDelete.mac: See, copy, edit or delete a saved password. Showing and copying ask macOS to verify you.
passwords.saveAllPasswordsToA.mac: Save all passwords to a CSV file after macOS verifies you.
setup.default.detailRequested.mac: Confirm Acira as your default browser, then come back.
local.workspaceHeaderDetail: Keep the workspace name, profile and cover controls together.
local.torWindowsAvailability: Bundled Tor is currently available in the Windows build. Proxy and secure DNS settings are in Privacy.
local.torTabsUnsupported: Tor tabs are available in the Windows build. You can use a regular private tab here.
local.torWindowsUnsupported: Tor windows are available in the Windows build. You can use a regular private window here.
local.verificationUnavailable: Password verification isn’t available on this system.
local.touchIdRequired: Set up Touch ID on this Mac to show, copy, edit or export saved passwords.
local.touchIdCancelled: Touch ID did not verify you. Your passwords stayed protected.
local.proxyVisibility: A proxy only moves your traffic; the proxy’s owner can see it.
local.webAppInstalledFinder: Installed {name}. It’s in Finder and Favorites.
local.macVerificationCancelled: macOS did not verify you. Your protected items stayed locked.
privacy.protectionsActive: {count, plural, one {# protection active. Each one has its own switch below.} other {# protections active. Each one has its own switch below.}}
privacy.readingProtection: Reading what this copy of Acira is running…
privacy.cookiesDetail: Blocked by the engine on every site. Embedded sign-in or payment frames may need Allow. Applies after restart.
privacy.listsDetail: Checked at start and every few hours, from easylist.to, ublockorigin.github.io and pgl.yoyo.org; only what changed is downloaded. Checked before use; the previous set is kept.
privacy.httpsDetail: Upgrade sites to HTTPS. If one has none, Acira asks before using HTTP for that tab. Reload open pages after changing it.
privacy.proxyOnDetail: Every site in this profile goes through your proxy. Calls (WebRTC) are kept from revealing your own address while it is on.
privacy.proxyVpnDetail: Use my VPN app: Acira follows your computer’s connection, a VPN included. Nothing to set here; turn the VPN on in its own app.
privacy.proxyTypeDetail: SOCKS5 proxies that ask for a username and password cannot be used; choose an HTTP proxy, or run your provider’s app and pick Use my VPN app.
privacy.addressDetail: Host and port, without a path or credentials. An HTTP proxy that needs a sign-in asks for it when a page loads; it is not saved.
privacy.testDetail: Connects to the proxy only, not to any website.
privacy.applyDetail: The current route is unconfirmed. Choose a setting and apply it.
privacy.vpnProvidersDetail: Acira has no VPN of its own and no deal with any provider. These three publish independent security audits. Acira earns nothing from these links and adds nothing to them.
privacy.clearNote: Bookmarks and downloaded files are never removed here.
privacy.timeRangeAllOnly: Cookies, site storage and cached files can only be cleared for all time.
privacy.timeRangeShort: History and download records can be cleared for a shorter time.
update.readyTipHint: Install it now or decide later.
update.readyBody: The new version is downloaded. Install now and Acira restarts into it, with your tabs and profile as they were.
report.row: Report a problem with this site
report.title: Report a problem
report.nothingElse: Nothing else: not the page's address, your history, cookies or accounts. Acira doesn't keep your IP address.
report.unavailable: Reports can't be sent from this window.
report.thanks: Thanks, the Acira team will look at it.
report.failed: The report couldn't be sent. Check your connection and try again.
report.tryLater: The report couldn't be sent right now. Try again later.
report.siteGone: The site is no longer open in this tab. Open it again, then send the report.
report.safeLink: This site is safe? Tell Acira
report.notePlaceholderApp: What happened, or your idea. Don't include personal details.
report.nothingElseApp: Nothing else: not the sites you visit, your history, cookies or accounts. Acira doesn't keep your IP address.
sidebar.sideDetail: Put the sidebar on the left or the right of the window.
windowview.edgeSideRight: Show the sidebar at the right edge
windowview.closedSidebarEdgeRight: Show the closed sidebar at the right edge
windowview.firstRunRight: Seamless is on. Point at the top or right edge for the toolbar or sidebar. Leave with {shortcut}.
sidebarmenu.title: Sidebar actions
windowview.closedSidebarEdgeDetailRight: Rest the pointer at the right edge to see a closed sidebar. Each window view has its own switch.
sidebar.sizeDetail: How much room the sidebar takes. Drag its edge and it settles on the nearest size.
sidebar.tabGroupsDetail: With tabs in the sidebar, where tab groups sit in the list: among the tabs in the order they were opened, or in an area of their own above or below the loose tabs.
sidebar.tabGroupsSearch: Keep tab groups with your tabs or in their own area

livepr.note.filtered: The filters hide every pull request.
livepr.note.rateLimited: GitHub asked Acira to wait a while.
livepr.menu.title: Pull requests
livepr.menu.author: Created by me
livepr.menu.repositoriesNote: Only repositories that have a pull request for you are listed.
livepr.add.title: Add a live folder for pull requests?
livepr.add.body1: Acira will ask github.com for your pull requests every few minutes while it is open, using the github.com sign-in this profile already has.
livepr.add.body2: It does not use Acira's servers, and Acira keeps no GitHub password or token.
